# Nordic trees — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/nordic-trees.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/nordic-trees.ttl`](../decks/nordic-trees.ttl) · **Cards:** 46 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

46 trees and shrubs that grow wild in Sweden and the Nordic countries or are widely planted there: conifers such as spruce, pine, juniper, yew and larches, and broadleaves such as birches, alders, aspen, oaks, beech, ash, elms, limes, maples, rowan, cherries and willows. Front: the English name and the Swedish name; back: the scientific name, as accepted by Dyntaxa, the Swedish taxonomic database (September 2026), with a note where another checklist uses a different name. Names from Dyntaxa and Wikidata, checked against Kew's World Checklist of Vascular Plants and Wikipedia.

## Licensing

The deck is released under CC0 1.0. Its content comes from two CC0 sources: Wikidata (structured data released under CC0) for the item behind every card, its taxon name, its English and Swedish labels and aliases and its taxon common names (P1843), and Dyntaxa (published by SLU Artdatabanken on GBIF under CC0 1.0) for the accepted scientific names, the Swedish names, English names and the synonyms in the notes. Every scientific and Swedish name on the cards is present verbatim in Dyntaxa; 45 English names are a Wikidata label, alias or taxon common name or a Dyntaxa English name, in some cases in different letter case. The one exception is 'Field elm' (Ulmus minor), which is in no CC0 or public-domain source the research found: it rests on the compiler's general knowledge and is one of the established common names of the species (a short name, not copyrightable expression), chosen so that it identifies the species without clashing with another card, and confirmed in the English Wikipedia and the GBIF Backbone Taxonomy's vernacular names. The note that Kew's WCVP and the Catalogue of Life place the Swedish whitebeam in Hedlundia is a single fact about those checklists, stated with attribution to them in the compiler's own words; the CC0 Wikidata item for the name Hedlundia intermedia supports the name itself. Kew's World Checklist of Vascular Plants, the Catalogue of Life and the GBIF Backbone Taxonomy (CC BY 4.0) and the English and Swedish Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0) were used for verification only: they confirmed names and facts, and no text, list or selection was copied from them (the notes are the compiler's own wording). The selection of species is the authoring agent's own. All verification sources are still credited in the deck's provenance and in this report.

## Method

1. Process. Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.
2. Authority. The library editor asked for about 45 Nordic trees and large shrubs with the scientific name on the back, one stated authority for accepted names, and notes on recent name changes. Dyntaxa, the Swedish taxonomic database kept by SLU Artdatabanken, was chosen as the single authority for the scientific name and the Swedish name, because it is the reference for Swedish names and is published under CC0 (on GBIF, dataset version 2026-09-29). Kew's World Checklist of Vascular Plants (WCVP, the data behind Plants of the World Online) was used as the independent international check. Plants of the World Online itself and its terms page answered HTTP 403 to the research environment, so WCVP was read through its GBIF copy (dataset version 2026-06-04, CC BY 4.0). Den virtuella floran (Naturhistoriska riksmuseet, linnaeus.nrm.se) could not be reached (connection refused on https, 404 on http) and SAOL at svenska.se only returns a JavaScript application to a script, so neither was used (the SAOL request, one per Swedish front, is among the queries; it returned only the application page, so no headword was found and nothing was used). The USDA PLANTS database (a US federal, public-domain source) was tried for English names through its profile API; it too returned only a JavaScript application page, so nothing was used; the Swedish names rest on Dyntaxa, checked against Wikidata and the Swedish Wikipedia.
3. Candidates. The authoring agent wrote down 77 candidate scientific names of trees and large shrubs that grow wild in the Nordic countries or are commonly planted there (forestry, parks, hedges), from general knowledge, together with the newer and older names it expected to meet (Scandosorbus intermedia, Hedlundia hybrida, Torminalis glaberrima, Salix euxina, Padus avium, Tilia × vulgaris …) to see how each source treats them (file candidates.txt).
4. Wikidata (content source). One SPARQL query (the first query below) fetched, for every candidate name, the items with that taxon name (P225), their taxon rank (P105), English and Swedish labels and aliases, Dyntaxa ID (P1939) and POWO ID (P5037). For the 46 species kept, the entity API (wbgetentities, labels, aliases, claims and sitelinks in en, sv and mul) was then read for the exact label and alias strings, the P225 and P1939 statements and the English and Swedish Wikipedia sitelinks (script fetch_wiki.py).
5. Dyntaxa (content source, authority). A first pass used GBIF's full-text species search restricted to the Dyntaxa dataset (script fetch.py); it missed some exact names among many subspecies and cultivar records, so the second pass (script fetch_dyntaxa.py) looked each candidate up by exact name in the dataset (GBIF /species?datasetKey=…&name=…, falling back to the search) and kept only records whose canonical name equals the candidate. For each record it fetched the vernacular names with GBIF's 'preferred' flag (languages swe and eng) and, for accepted records, the synonyms. Every one of the 46 species has exactly one ACCEPTED record of rank SPECIES under the card's name (Tilia ×europaea was found under its canonical form 'Tilia europaea').
6. WCVP (verification). Each candidate name was looked up the same way in the WCVP dataset on GBIF (script fetch_wcvp.py). For each card the WCVP record with exactly Dyntaxa's scientific name including the author was compared: 45 are ACCEPTED in WCVP under the same name and author; Sorbus intermedia (Ehrh.) Pers. is a SYNONYM of Hedlundia intermedia in WCVP. Other candidates where the two checklists differ were left out (see the selection).
7. Wikipedia (verification). The introductions of the English and Swedish articles linked from each Wikidata item were fetched with the MediaWiki API (TextExtracts, plain text, with the revision id; script fetch_wiki.py), and the sentence naming the card's English or Swedish name was picked by script (sentences.py; two English sentences that the simple splitter cut at an abbreviation were taken whole by hand from the same saved extract). Each quote is in the card's evidence with a link to its revision.
8. Card text. Back: Dyntaxa's accepted scientific name without author, tagged as Latin; it is also the Wikidata taxon name (P225) for 45 cards (for the hybrid lime Wikidata writes 'Tilia × europaea' with a space; the card follows Dyntaxa and WCVP, 'Tilia ×europaea', the form the botanical Code recommends, and the note gives the spaced form). Swedish front: Dyntaxa's preferred Swedish name, in lower case, for 45 cards; for Larix decidua Dyntaxa's preferred name is just 'lärk', which would not tell it from Siberian larch in the same deck, so the card uses Dyntaxa's other name 'europeisk lärk' (also a Wikidata alias and in the Swedish Wikipedia's first sentence) and says so in a note. English front: a name that identifies the species, chosen among the English names in Wikidata (label or alias) and Dyntaxa, written in sentence case (capital first letter, proper names such as Norway, Scots, Sitka, Douglas and Swedish capitalised), and confirmed in the English Wikipedia introduction. Generic names were avoided where they would be ambiguous (European aspen rather than aspen, European elder rather than elder, Sycamore maple rather than sycamore, which in North America is a plane tree). Two English fronts are not a label or alias under Wikidata's plain 'en' language code nor a Dyntaxa English name, but are Wikidata taxon common names (P1843), a CC0 source: 'European white elm' for Ulmus laevis (P1843 'European White Elm'@en) and 'Sycamore maple' for Acer pseudoplatanus ('Sycamore maple' is only an en-us alias and a P1843 value, 'sycamore maple'@en). One English front rests on the compiler's general knowledge: for Ulmus minor the CC0 sources give only 'Small-leaved elm' (which would read like Small-leaved lime, another card), and the card gives 'Field elm', one of the species' established English names, confirmed in the English Wikipedia introduction and in the vernacular names the GBIF Backbone Taxonomy collects (Catalogue of Life, IUCN Red List and others; the public-domain GRIN Taxonomy has 'European field elm'). In the first draft only the Wikidata labels and aliases were compared, so these three were all recorded as having no CC0 source; quality-control round 1 found the taxon common names (see licensing). No Swedish text was translated by the agent: every Swedish front is a Dyntaxa name.
9. Notes. A back note, in the compiler's own words, was written where it helps: the short Swedish names ek, lind, lönn and alm (other Swedish names in Dyntaxa, Wikidata sv labels or aliases; the Swedish Wikipedia confirms them), the other Swedish names fågelbär, skogsolvon and enbuske (Dyntaxa or Wikidata, and the Swedish Wikipedia), the British name sycamore (Wikidata en and en-gb aliases and taxon common names; the GBIF Backbone's UK Species Inventory name; English Wikipedia), the hybrid lime and its synonym Tilia ×vulgaris (Dyntaxa synonyms and English Wikipedia), the former name Rhamnus frangula (Dyntaxa synonym; the Swedish Wikipedia still uses it), the placement of the Swedish whitebeam in Hedlundia by WCVP and the Catalogue of Life (the name Hedlundia intermedia is a separate Wikidata item; the placement is a single fact, stated with attribution to the two checklists) and the Dyntaxa main name lärk. Words cited in the notes are in quotation marks, “ ” in English and ” ” in Swedish (Språkrådet's Svenska skrivregler).
10. Cross-checks and machine checks. The generator script (gen.py) builds every card's evidence from the saved raw responses and asserts that each card has exactly one accepted Dyntaxa species record, exactly one WCVP record with the same name and author, and that each quoted Wikipedia sentence occurs verbatim in the saved extract. It adds a Wikidata check of the taxon name (P225) wherever it equals the card's back (45 cards), of the Dyntaxa ID (P1939) wherever it equals the Dyntaxa taxon id (45 cards), and of the English and Swedish names as label or alias wherever Wikidata has the card's text in exactly its letter case; the builder runs them against live Wikidata on every build. Differences in letter case only (many Wikidata English names are lower case and many Swedish labels start with a capital) are listed under quality control.
11. Quality-control round 1 (independent AI reviewers). The deck's scope was widened from 'trees and large shrubs' to 'trees and shrubs', because dwarf birch (Betula nana) is a low shrub; the notes were put in quotation marks and the 'everyday' wording of four notes neutralised; the juniper card got a note on 'enbuske'; Wikidata taxon common names and aliases, the Catalogue of Life and the GBIF Backbone Taxonomy's vernacular names were added as evidence, with new Wikidata checks; the queries of round 1 are listed among the queries.
12. Scripts. The helper scripts named here (fetch.py, fetch_dyntaxa.py, fetch_wcvp.py, fetch_wiki.py, sentences.py, gen.py, saol.py, usda.py) are not published; this method describes what each did, and the queries list gives every URL template and query they sent.

## Selection

The deck has 46 species of trees and shrubs that are native to Sweden and the other Nordic countries or widely planted there: the main forest trees (Norway spruce, Scots pine, silver and downy birch, aspen, alders), the broadleaved trees of the south (oaks, beech, hornbeam, ash, elms, limes, maples, wild cherry, crab apple, Swedish whitebeam), common trees and shrubs of woods, hedges and shores (hazel, rowan, bird cherry, blackthorn, hawthorn, alder buckthorn, goat, white and bay willow, juniper, yew, elder, holly, guelder rose, and dwarf birch, a low shrub of the mountains and bogs, kept as one of the most characteristic woody plants of the Nordic fells; the deck's scope was widened from 'trees and large shrubs' to 'trees and shrubs' for it in quality-control round 1) and the most planted non-native trees (European and Siberian larch, lodgepole pine, Sitka spruce, Douglas fir, white poplar, horse chestnut, common lime, sycamore maple). Inclusion criteria: (1) an ACCEPTED species (or, for the common lime, nothospecies) in Dyntaxa under the card's name; (2) the same name and author in Kew's WCVP, accepted or with the difference stated in a note; (3) a Wikidata item with that taxon name and the Swedish name as label or alias (letter case aside); (4) an English name that identifies the species. The candidates were drafted by the authoring agent from general knowledge (no published list was copied) and cut to 46 by the agent's judgement of how familiar a tree is in the Nordic countries. Left out because of naming or taxonomy: Salix fragilis/knäckepil (Dyntaxa now gives knäckepil as Salix euxina and Salix ×fragilis as grönpil, the English 'crack willow' covers both, and the Wikidata item 'Salix fragilis' mixes them); Sorbus hybrida/finnoxel and Sorbus torminalis/tyskoxel (Dyntaxa keeps them in Sorbus, WCVP has Hedlundia hybrida and Aria torminalis, and Wikidata has separate items for the new names); Sorbus aria (WCVP: a synonym of Aria edulis; rare in the Nordic countries); Picea glauca (WCVP: a synonym of Picea laxa); Hippophae rhamnoides/havtorn (Dyntaxa spells the accepted name Hippophaë rhamnoides, WCVP and Wikidata Hippophae: the back would differ between sources); Salix cinerea (Dyntaxa separates the species from an aggregate of the same name); Tilia × vulgaris and Ulmus × hollandica (no Dyntaxa species record under that name; T. ×vulgaris is a Dyntaxa synonym of T. ×europaea). Left out only to keep the deck near the requested size: Rhamnus cathartica, Euonymus europaeus, Prunus cerasus, Salix viminalis, Populus nigra, Pinus mugo, Pinus cembra, Abies alba, Abies sibirica, Abies lasiocarpa, Larix kaempferi, Thuja plicata, Myrica gale. Genera (Cotoneaster), subspecies (e.g. mountain birch, Betula pubescens subsp. czerepanovii), cultivars and aggregates are not included.

## Queries

**Candidate species: item, rank, English and Swedish labels and aliases, Dyntaxa ID and POWO ID for 77 candidate names (POST to https://query.wikidata.org/sparql, format json; script fetch.py)** (Wikidata: the items of the 46 species (taxon name P225, taxon common name P1843, Dyntaxa ID P1939, English and Swedish labels and aliases) and the item of Hedlundia intermedia)

```
SELECT ?name ?item ?rank ?en ?sv (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ?enAlt; separator="|") AS ?enAlts) (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ?svAlt; separator="|") AS ?svAlts) (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ?dyntaxa; separator="|") AS ?dyn) (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ?powo; separator="|") AS ?powos) WHERE {
  VALUES ?name { "Picea abies" "Pinus sylvestris" "Betula pendula" "Betula pubescens" "Betula nana" "Alnus glutinosa" "Alnus incana" "Populus tremula" "Populus alba" "Quercus robur" "Quercus petraea" "Fagus sylvatica" "Fraxinus excelsior" "Ulmus glabra" "Ulmus laevis" "Ulmus minor" "Tilia cordata" "Tilia platyphyllos" "Tilia × europaea" "Tilia ×europaea" "Tilia europaea" "Tilia × vulgaris" "Acer platanoides" "Acer pseudoplatanus" "Acer campestre" "Sorbus aucuparia" "Sorbus intermedia" "Scandosorbus intermedia" "Sorbus hybrida" "Hedlundia hybrida" "Sorbus torminalis" "Torminalis glaberrima" "Salix caprea" "Salix alba" "Salix pentandra" "Salix fragilis" "Salix euxina" "Salix × fragilis" "Salix cinerea" "Juniperus communis" "Taxus baccata" "Larix decidua" "Larix sibirica" "Larix kaempferi" "Prunus padus" "Padus avium" "Prunus avium" "Malus sylvestris" "Carpinus betulus" "Corylus avellana" "Frangula alnus" "Rhamnus cathartica" "Crataegus monogyna" "Aesculus hippocastanum" "Pinus contorta" "Picea sitchensis" "Pseudotsuga menziesii" "Abies alba" "Hippophae rhamnoides" "Sambucus nigra" "Ilex aquifolium" "Viburnum opulus" "Euonymus europaeus" "Prunus spinosa" "Myrica gale" "Pinus cembra" "Thuja plicata" "Populus nigra" "Pinus mugo" "Picea glauca" "Abies sibirica" "Abies lasiocarpa" "Sorbus aria" "Cotoneaster" "Prunus cerasus" "Salix viminalis" "Ulmus × hollandica" }
  ?item wdt:P225 ?name ; wdt:P105 ?rank .
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?en FILTER(LANG(?en) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item rdfs:label ?sv FILTER(LANG(?sv) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item skos:altLabel ?enAlt FILTER(LANG(?enAlt) = "en") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item skos:altLabel ?svAlt FILTER(LANG(?svAlt) = "sv") }
  OPTIONAL { ?item wdt:P1939 ?dyntaxa }
  OPTIONAL { ?item wdt:P5037 ?powo }
} GROUP BY ?name ?item ?rank ?en ?sv
```

**First pass (script fetch.py): full-text search in the Dyntaxa dataset for each candidate ({name} URL-encoded), with the vernacular names and synonyms of the hits; superseded by the exact-name pass below** (Dyntaxa. Svensk taxonomisk databas (via GBIF, dataset version of 2026-09-29))

```
https://api.gbif.org/v1/species/search?datasetKey=de8934f4-a136-481c-a87a-b0b202b80a31&q={name}&limit=50
```

**Dyntaxa dataset metadata on GBIF (licence, publication date, citation)** (Dyntaxa. Svensk taxonomisk databas (via GBIF, dataset version of 2026-09-29))

```
curl -sS -L -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o gbif-dyntaxa-dataset.json https://api.gbif.org/v1/dataset/de8934f4-a136-481c-a87a-b0b202b80a31
```

**Exact-name lookup of each candidate in Dyntaxa (script fetch_dyntaxa.py); records kept only when the canonical name equals the candidate; when it returns nothing, the search URL of the first pass with limit=100** (Dyntaxa. Svensk taxonomisk databas (via GBIF, dataset version of 2026-09-29))

```
https://api.gbif.org/v1/species?datasetKey=de8934f4-a136-481c-a87a-b0b202b80a31&name={name}&limit=50
```

**Vernacular names (language, name, preferred flag) of each matching Dyntaxa record** (Dyntaxa. Svensk taxonomisk databas (via GBIF, dataset version of 2026-09-29))

```
https://api.gbif.org/v1/species/{key}/vernacularNames?limit=50
```

**Synonyms of each accepted Dyntaxa record** (Dyntaxa. Svensk taxonomisk databas (via GBIF, dataset version of 2026-09-29))

```
https://api.gbif.org/v1/species/{key}/synonyms?limit=100
```

**Plants of the World Online terms page and API (both answered HTTP 403; nothing used)** (The World Checklist of Vascular Plants (WCVP), the checklist behind Plants of the World Online (via GBIF, dataset version of 2026-06-04))

```
curl -sS -L -A "Mozilla/5.0 (solid-memo deck research; https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o powo-terms.html https://powo.science.kew.org/terms-and-conditions ; curl -sS -L -A "Mozilla/5.0 (solid-memo deck research; https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o powo-picea.json "https://powo.science.kew.org/api/2/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:262609-1"
```

**Finding the WCVP dataset on GBIF** (The World Checklist of Vascular Plants (WCVP), the checklist behind Plants of the World Online (via GBIF, dataset version of 2026-06-04))


## Quality control

5 rounds, 24 findings: 18 fixed, 0 rejected after checking, 6 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (135 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

### Round 0: Sources and machine checks: every card's scientific, Swedish and English names compared across Dyntaxa, WCVP, Wikidata and the English and Swedish Wikipedia. (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — authoring agent, machine checks · **Scope:** All 46 cards and the candidates left out.

All 46 scientific names are Dyntaxa's accepted name; 45 are accepted in WCVP under the same name and author (Sorbus intermedia is a WCVP synonym of Hedlundia intermedia, noted on the card). 45 equal the Wikidata taxon name (P225) and 45 items carry the card's Dyntaxa taxon id (P1939): both checked by the builder. All Swedish fronts are Dyntaxa names and appear in the first sentences of the Swedish Wikipedia articles; 43 English fronts are a Wikidata label or alias or a Dyntaxa English name (letter case aside) and all 46 appear in the English Wikipedia introduction. ### Round 1: Factual accuracy (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent Factual accuracy reviewer · **Scope:** All 46 cards, the description and the selection, re-checked against the Catalogue of Life, the GBIF Backbone Taxonomy, Dyntaxa and WCVP on GBIF, Wikidata and Wikipedia.

Every card's fact was confirmed; the only problem was scope: dwarf birch is a low shrub, not a tree or a large shrub as the description said. The scope is now 'trees and shrubs'. The suggestion on the Hedlundia note was applied, citing the Catalogue of Life.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| dwarf-birch | The description and selection say 'trees and large shrubs', but Betula nana is a low shrub growing up to about 1–1.2 m (English Wikipedia), so the deck's stated scope does not cover the card. | Verified (English Wikipedia's Betula nana: 'a monoecious, deciduous shrub growing up to 1–1.2 metres'). The card is kept (it is correct, and dwarf birch is one of the most characteristic woody plants of the Nordic fells); the description now says '46 trees and shrubs' / '46 träd och buskar', and the selection explains the wider scope. The suggested height note was not added, because the height is given only by a verification source (English Wikipedia), and the builder's policy lets a verification source only confirm what a content source gave. | fixed |
| swedish-whitebeam | The note names only Kew's WCVP for the Hedlundia placement; the Catalogue of Life also treats Sorbus intermedia as a synonym of Hedlundia intermedia. | Verified in the Catalogue of Life release 2026-09-11 (ChecklistBank 3LR, name usage 6YW2K: synonym of Hedlundia intermedia (Ehrh.) Mosyakin, Fedor. & McNeill). The note now names both checklists, and the Catalogue of Life is a new verification source with its evidence on the card. | fixed |
